title: Utility Order for Cleco Power LLC, ex parte. — This order requires the Administrative Hearings Division to serve as hearing examiner in this docket, to compile a complete evidentiary record with no formal recommendation, and to establish a procedural schedule that provides for Commission consideration of this matter at the March 2027 Business and Executive Session.  This matter was considered at the Commission's September 16, 2026 Business and Executive Session.

LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                     ORDER NUMBER U-38035

                               CLECO POWER LLC, EX PARTE.

Docket No. U-38035, In re: Application of Cleco Power LLC for authorization of certain
contracts, including a site specific contract, as well as certification of transmission
interconnection, new generation, and associated waivers for a large load customer pursuant
to the Commission's Lightning Initiative.

               (Decided at the September 16, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


    I.      OVERVIEW AND PROCEDURAL HISTORY
         On July 1, 2026, Cleco Power LLC (“Cleco” or the “Company”) filed its application

for authorization of certain contracts and certification of transmission interconnection, new

generation, and associated waivers for a large load customer (the “Application”).                       The

Application was filed pursuant to the Louisiana Public Service Commission’s (“Commission”

or “LPSC”) Lightning Directive, adopted at the December 17, 2025 Business and Executive

Session. The Lightning Directive provided for certain waivers of the Commission’s Market

Based Mechanism Order (“MBM Order”)1 for a proposed capacity addition where certain

factors are demonstrated. The Lightning Directive also directed Staff to take reasonable steps

to ensure that the applications filed under the directive are reviewed and processed on a timely

basis, with the objective of the Commission being able to vote within 8 months of an

application.

         The Application was noticed in the Commission’s Official Bulletin #1380 dated July

17, 2026. Interventions were filed by Pelican Power LLC, Packaging Corporation of America,

the Alliance for Affordable Energy, Sierra Club, Southern Renewable Energy Association, and

International Paper Company, and interested party status was granted to Cabot Corporation,

Entergy Louisiana, LLC, and Southwestern Electric Power Company (together, with Staff and

the Company, “the Parties”).

         The Application sought, among other things, Commission certification of a new

combined cycle gas turbine (“CCGT”) generation resource and confirmation of regulatory

treatment applicable to certain transmission interconnection facilities necessary to reliably


1 General Order dated October 14, 2024 (R-34247). In re: Rulemaking to consider changes to Commission General

Order dated October 29, 2008 (Docket No. R-26172 Subdocket C) (“Market Based Mechanisms Order”) to
incorporate formal complaint procedures. This Order combines, amends, and supersedes previous General Orders
in dockets: R-36172-C, R-34003, R-35462, and R-34247. This Order also amends and supersedes General Order
dated October 29, 2008.

                                                                                      Order No. U-38035
                                                                                                 Page 1
 serve Cleco Power’s existing customers and a new customer, Applied Digital Corporation (the

“Customer”), and the Customer’s hyperscale data center project that will be located in Rapides

Parish, Louisiana (the “Project”). The Project’s load is expected to be approximately 430

megawatts by 2028, representing a substantial, long-term addition to Cleco Power’s retail load,

for which the Company proposes to provide electrical service pursuant to an Electric Service

Agreement (“ESA”).

        In its Application, Cleco asserted that it’s Application meets the Lightning

Amendment’s criteria for timely review and processing.2 Cleco also requested timely treatment

as the Company has entered into a Capacity Agreement with Tenaska Frontier Partners, Ltd.

(“Tenaska Agreement”), to support the Project before new, long-term generation can be

constructed and placed in service and to support the Company’s resource adequacy obligations.

The Tenaska Agreement term runs from the effective date through May 31, 2037, covering 10

MISO Planning Years, beginning with the 2027-2028 Planning Year starting June 1, 2027.

Thus, per the terms of the Tenaska Agreement, Cleco contends that it is critical for the Company

to obtain timely approval of the Application, including the Tenaska Agreement, no later than

the Commission’s March 2027 Business and Executive meeting.

        After much discussion, the Parties convened at a status conference held on August 25,

2026 to present a proposed procedural schedule to the Administrative Law Judge (“ALJ”).

The Parties and the ALJ were unable to set a procedural schedule due to the expedited

timeframe needed to meet both the Lightning Initiative and the Tenaska Agreement, while

allowing enough time for the ALJ to make a formal recommendation.

        On September 1, 2026, the Cleco filed its Motion Pursuant to Rule 57 for Procedural

Directive (“Motion”) wherein the Company requested the Commission exercise its original and

primary jurisdiction, pursuant to Rule 57 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure,

and issue an Order directing the Administrative Hearings Division to adopt a procedural

schedule in this matter to ensure that the Application be reviewed and processed on a timely

basis and to facilitate Commission vote on the Application’s requests within eight (8) months

of the Application’s filing, or at the March 2027 Business and Executive Session. Cleco Power

further requested the Commission issue an Order directing the Administrative Hearings




2 Direct testimony of Cleco Power witness D. Andrew Owens at p. 10, line 14 – page 12, line 11.



                                                                                       Order No. U-38035
                                                                                                  Page 2
 Division to serve as hearing examiner and compile a complete evidentiary record of this

proceeding, without the issuance of a formal recommendation, for the Commission’s de novo

consideration.

           Due to the Parties’ inability to set a procedural schedule, Staff did not oppose the

Motion.


    II.       COMMISSION JURISDICTION

           The jurisdiction of the Commission is set forth by constitutional and statutory

provisions. The Louisiana Constitution, Article IV, Section 21, provides:

                  The Commission shall regulate all common carriers and public
                  utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by
                  law. It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations, and
                  procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and shall
                  have other powers and perform other duties as provided by law.


    III.      COMMISSION CONSIDERATION

    The matter was considered at the Commission’s September 16, 2026 Business and

Executive Session. On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Vice Chairman Coussan,

and unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to exercise its original and primary

jurisdiction pursuant to Rule 57.

    After discussion,3 on motion of Commissioner Francis, seconded by Chairman Skrmetta,

and unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to direct the Administrative Hearings

Division to establish a procedural schedule in LPSC Docket No. U-38035 that provides for

Commission consideration of the Application no later than the March 2027 Business and

Executive Session; and direct the Administrative Hearings Division to serve as hearing

examiner and compile a complete evidentiary record for the Commission’s de novo

consideration, without the issuance of a formal recommendation from the presiding

Administrative Law Judge.



THEREFORE, IT IS ORDERED:

            1.    The Administrative Hearings Division shall establish a
                  procedural schedule in LPSC Docket No. U-38035 that provides
                  for Commission consideration of the Application no later than
                  the March 2027 Business and Executive Session.



3 The Parties did not voice opposition during the discussion at the B&E.



                                                                              Order No. U-38035
                                                                                         Page 3
      2.   The Administrative Hearings Division shall serve as hearing
          examiner and compile a complete evidentiary record for the
          Commission’s de novo consideration, without the issuance of a
          formal recommendation from the presiding Administrative Law
          Judge.



BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA
October 15, 2026
